hook.line: Nobody in Bogotá says "we'll meet at exactly nine". They say about nine, or the start of the month, and leave a little room. Spanish has set phrases for that room.
hook.es: Llegamos a eso de las nueve.

examples.es: Llegamos a eso de las nueve.
A finales de mes no queda plata.
examples.en: By the end of the month there's no money left.

examples.es: Nos mudamos a principios de año.
examples.en: We moved at the beginning of the year.

examples.es: La obra termina a mediados de marzo.
examples.en: The building work finishes in mid-March.

examples.es: Vale abre el café a eso de las siete.
examples.en: Vale opens the café at about seven.

examples.es: La gente de Altamira vuelve a principios de mes.
examples.en: The Altamira people come back at the beginning of the month.

rule:
To say "about" a clock time, use *a eso de* before the hour: *a eso de las nueve*. It is not exact, and that is the point.

To point at part of a month or a year, use *a* plus a word for where you are in it, then *de*:

*a principios de* = at the beginning of
*a mediados de* = in the middle of
*a finales de* = at the end of

After *de* comes the month or period: *a principios de año*, *a mediados de marzo*, *a finales de mes*.

English uses "around", "early", "mid" and "late", all in different spots. Spanish keeps one shape: *a ... de*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these approximating adverbial phrases. *A eso de* means "around"; *a principios, mediados, finales de* locate a moment inside a period.

readAndPick.es: Llegamos a eso de las nueve.
options: We arrived at exactly nine.
We arrived at about nine.
We arrived after nine.

readAndPick.es: A finales de mes no queda plata.
options: At the start of the month there's no money left.
In the middle of the month there's no money left.
By the end of the month there's no money left.

readAndPick.es: Nos mudamos a principios de año.
options: We moved at the beginning of the year.
We moved at the end of the year.
We moved in the middle of the year.

readAndPick.es: La obra termina a mediados de marzo.
options: The work finishes at the start of March.
The work finishes in mid-March.
The work finishes at the end of March.

readAndPick.es: Vale abre el café a eso de las siete.
options: Vale opens the café at seven sharp.
Vale opens the café at about seven.
Vale closes the café at about seven.

readAndPick.es: La gente de Altamira vuelve a principios de mes.
options: The Altamira people come back at the end of the month.
The Altamira people come back in the middle of the month.
The Altamira people come back at the beginning of the month.

readAndPick.es: Nos vemos a eso de las tres.
options: See you at about three.
See you at exactly three.
We saw each other at three.
I finish at the beginning of the year.
I finish at the end of the year.
I finish in the middle of the year.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right phrase and type the whole sentence: *Llegamos ___ las nueve.* (a eso de or en)
yourTurn.answer: Llegamos a eso de las nueve.
yourTurn.why: *A eso de* is the "about" before a clock time.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: By the end of the month there's no money left.
yourTurn.answer: A finales de mes no queda plata.
yourTurn.why: *A finales de* plus the period gives "by the end of".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We moved at the beginning of the year.
yourTurn.answer: Nos mudamos a principios de año.
yourTurn.why: *A principios de* means "at the beginning of".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The building work finishes in mid-March.
yourTurn.answer: La obra termina a mediados de marzo.
yourTurn.why: *A mediados de* means "in the middle of".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Vale opens the café at about seven.
yourTurn.answer: Vale abre el café a eso de las siete.
yourTurn.why: *A eso de las* plus the hour keeps the time approximate.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about the start: *La gente de Altamira vuelve a finales de mes.* Say: The Altamira people come back at the beginning of the month.
yourTurn.answer: La gente de Altamira vuelve a principios de mes.
yourTurn.why: Swap *finales* for *principios* to move to the start.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: See you at about three.
yourTurn.answer: Nos vemos a eso de las tres.
yourTurn.why: Same *a eso de las* frame, new hour.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Alrededor* needs *de* before the time, just like *a eso de*.

pitfalls.wrong: Nos mudamos a principios del año.
pitfalls.right: Nos mudamos a principios de año.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *a principios de* you don't need an article: *de año*.

pitfalls.right: Llegamos a eso de las nueve.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Clock times keep their *las*: *las nueve*.

personal: Say roughly when something happens in your week or year, with *a eso de las* or *a principios de*.
